newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE STOCKS SEEN DRAWING BARGAIN HUNTERS.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE STOCKS SEEN DRAWING BARGAIN HUNTERS.

text.p: Singapore shares are likely to draw some bargain-hunting interest on Tuesday after tumbling to four-year lows in active trading on Monday, dealers said.
On Monday, the benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index (STII) ended 2.58 percent lower at 1,893.86, down 50.06 points.
Dealers said there was relatively strong support at 1,850 points although the market still maintained a negative bias.
"There's been a lot of redemption from overseas funds but I also have many buy programmes in place," a local bank dealer said, noting the presence of bargain hunters.
Investors were seen looking for "fair value" stocks and could be buying issues trading below their price earnings ratios, especially blue chips, dealers said.
